rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's twenty-two builder trees go (a row of jacarandas, ficus, eucalyptus and magnolias along the back fences, palms, a norfolk pine and magnolias 3-3.5 m from the house fronts); five come back on their own spots, about one for every two houses: by the grill, the patio set, the swing set, and two in the back yards 7-9 m from the houses.

trees.why: the back yard with the kettle grill (2.4 m off): a magnolia over the cook
the west back yard with the patio set (2.1 m off): a jacaranda over the table
the yard with the swing set (2.6 m off): shade over the swings
the east back yard of the south row, 7 m from the house: the one tree of the old back fence row there
the north back lot line, 9 m from the houses: an old ficus between two yards
